newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher after stocks firm.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher after stocks firm.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock index futures ended higher on Tuesday after a rebound in Tokyo shares, but sentiment remained cautious, dealers said.
The longer-term downtrend was still seen intact as Japanese banking woes kept investors shy of yen-based assets.

"Japanese investors are going into higher-yield currencies and markets. This will cap action on the Nikkei," a dealer with a U.S. brokerage said, noting that technicals were bearish and further hampered by poor performance in financial stocks.
June Nikkei brushed critical resistance at 18,000 points but pulled back to close at 17,945 on a volume of 13,030 lots.
Dealers said the index hit heavy resistance at 18,000 and next at 18,300 points.
Some had attributed Tuesday's Nikkei cash market vigour to demand for some blue-chip issues and a rebound in the Dow Jones.
The opening of books by companies for the new financial year was also cited as another reason for the firmer tone.
The MSCI Taiwan stock index finished weaker, failing to sustain early gains on the back of Wall Street's recovery.
The April contract ended 0.9 poins lower at 359.2 on a relatively healthy turnover of 1,398 lots.
